09:00.headline: Multi-sport or baseball only?
09:00.topic: Parent Debate: keep playing multiple sports vs. year-round baseball
09:00.caption:
Should your player keep playing other sports, or focus on baseball year-round?

It's one of the most common debates in baseball families, and both sides have real points.

A) Keep playing two or three sports
✅ Builds overall athleticism and movement skills
✅ A break from the same throwing and swinging motions
✅ He learns to compete in different settings

B) Year-round baseball
✅ More reps and more development time
✅ More chances to get measured and seen
✅ Time to build his numbers before recruiting heats up

You'll hear coaches and parents on both sides of this one. The right answer often depends on his age, his body and how much he loves each sport.

Which way did your family go, and what did you learn? Reply A or B and tell us why 👇

13:00.headline: How to break the tie
13:00.topic: Choosing between two interested schools: roster role, major, real cost after aid, daily coach
13:00.caption:
Two schools are interested in your player. Now what?

When the logo and the gut feeling don't settle it, these four questions help:

⚾ His role on the roster: How many players at his position are returning, and where would he fit? Ask the coach directly.
⚾ His major is offered: Confirm it's there and ask how players balance it with baseball.
⚾ Real cost after aid: Compare what your family would actually pay once any athletic, academic and need-based aid is counted, not the sticker price.
⚾ Who coaches him daily: Find out who works with his position group every day, not just who recruited him.

Comparing his numbers with typical ranges at each level can also show which program is the more realistic fit right now.
